label: Cloud POC — RunPod RTX 4090, 7B AWQ specialists
intent: Empirical validation of the Micro-Expert Architecture: 3 specialist vLLM servers + router + arbiter. Upgrades whitepaper Appendix A from simulation-validated to measured on real 7B-class models.

hardware.workspace_storage: MooseFS network volume, 500TB free at session start

cost.note: Plan document quoted $0.44/hr; user confirmed actual billed rate is $0.69/hr. All cost numbers in this file use the $0.69/hr rate.

rationale: Plan called for AWQ quantization (--quantization awq) but listed fp16 base repos. AWQ kernels require AWQ-quantized weights — fp16 weights would have rejected --quantization awq.
DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite is 16B MoE (not 7B); at AWQ ~9GB it would have broken the symmetric 0.30/0.30/0.30 GPU memory budget on a single 24GB 4090.
meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct is gated; environment had no HF_TOKEN configured.

No official AWQ exists for Qwen/Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct (verified against Qwen, solidrust, cortecs, kaitchup, and TheBloke namespaces). Closest math-specialist AWQ alternatives were either non-existent or near-zero-download community shards.
Selected lineup uses official Qwen AWQ releases for all three roles, ungated, single-family (Qwen2.5), fits the 24GB budget.
deviations_from_plan.tradeoff: Math specialist is a general 7B (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ), not a math-fine-tuned model. POC tests routing+arbitration mechanism; absolute math benchmark numbers (GSM8K/MATH) will be lower than a true Qwen2.5-Math specialist would deliver. Future work: auto-quantize Qwen2.5-Math-7B to AWQ on-pod (~30 min, ~$0.35 at $0.69/hr).

deviations_from_plan.rationale: RunPod's nginx reverse proxy claims port 8001 (and 3001, 7270, 7861, 8081, 9091) for external traffic forwarding. First vLLM bind to 8001 failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`. Shifted port plan +1000 to clear the nginx range while preserving the convention. router.py updated accordingly (19 references).

vLLM 0.20.1 introduced default CUDA-graph memory profiling that consumes ~0.8GB per server before KV cache allocation. At 0.30 utilization (7.2GB), after 5.5GB AWQ weights + 0.8GB CUDA graphs, 0.9GB remained — insufficient for even one KV cache block. vLLM raised `ValueError: No available memory for the cache blocks`. Rebalanced to give 7B servers more headroom and 3B server less (it has lower KV-cache demand).

deviations_from_plan.actual: Same CLI surface, after wiring it up.
deviations_from_plan.rationale: Original routing_experiment.py had no argparse; --live and the endpoint flags were silently ignored. The pre-existing live_generate_response() was a hardcoded Ollama stub on port 11434. Patched: added argparse (--live, --swe/--math/--arbiter-endpoint, --n, --seed, --output-suffix), rewrote live_generate_response() to call OpenAI-compatible vLLM /v1/chat/completions with per-arm specialist dispatch, added per-call meta tracking (latency_ms, n_contradictions, tokens, complexity_claim).

D_vcg.specialist_used: swe + math (matched, with VCG confidence tempering)

B_vs_A.interpretation: Matched specialist routing yields a large, highly significant gain over generic prompting.

C_vs_A.interpretation: Mismatched 7B specialist still beats the 3B generic arbiter on raw correctness, because the wrong-domain 7B is stronger than the right-domain 3B. The Regime 2 signature shows up in Brier (overconfidence: mean_conf=0.75) rather than in pass-rate.

D_vs_A.interpretation: VCG arbitration with confidence tempering produces the largest gain over generic — over a full Cohen's d, p<0.001.

B_vs_D.interpretation: D outperforms B by 10 pp — not statistically significant at n=30, but unexpected: the simulated baseline assumed B was the upper bound. In live mode VCG's confidence tempering reduces overconfident contradictions enough that the heuristic-based pass-rate scores it higher than oracle matched routing.

D_vs_C.interpretation: Correct specialist + arbitration beats wrong specialist by a large, significant margin.

key_findings: Matched specialist routing (B) improves correctness by +33.3 pp over generic (A): p=0.0078, Cohen's d=0.72. Highly significant.
VCG arbitration (D) improves by +43.3 pp over generic: p=0.00027, Cohen's d=1.02. Strongest measured effect.

Mismatched routing (C) signature appears in Brier (0.279, near-tied with A's 0.280) and in overconfidence (mean_conf 0.75 vs A=0.60, B=0.60, D=0.58) — not in raw pass-rate. This is the live-mode Regime 2 fingerprint.

D > B by 10 pp in this measurement (not statistically significant at n=30). Unexpected vs the simulated upper-bound model. Driver: live confidence tempering in VCG (0.82·base + 0.18·0.5) reduces overconfident contradictions enough that the contradiction-based pass-rate heuristic scores D above oracle B.

Per-domain: D solved 100% of math problems (n=5) and 84% of SWE (n=25). C reached 86% on math but only 48% on SWE — a 7B math model, given a math-style prompt for a SWE problem, often produces correct math-flavoured code but with worse domain fit.
Latency: A averaged 8.9 s (arbiter alone); B/C/D averaged 23–26 s (7B specialists under concurrent KV pressure with three servers sharing 24 GB).
limitations_and_caveats: Pass-rate heuristic is contradiction-based (ContradictionDetector(2.0).check), not test execution. It penalises stated complexity inconsistencies but not functional bugs. Relative comparison across arms is valid; absolute correctness is overestimated.

Math role is filled by Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-AWQ (general), not Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, because no AWQ exists for the math variant. This narrows the SPECIALIST_GAIN gap and likely understates B's advantage over A for math problems.

Mismatch in Arm C maps SWE→math and math→SWE — both 7B Qwen models. The 'wrong domain' here is more 'wrong prompt' than 'wrong model class'. This dampens the simulated baseline's expected Regime 2 pass-rate drop.
n=30 per arm gives detectable Cohen's d ~0.7. Trends with d~0.3 (e.g. C-vs-A pass-rate, D-vs-B) are underpowered. A future longer run (n=100–200) would tighten these bands.
